gap.docPath.markdownDescription: Path to the `doc/` directory, e.g. `C:\Program Files\GAP-4.16.1\runtime\opt\gap-4.16.1\doc` or `/opt/gap-4.16.1/doc`.

gap.pkgPath.markdownDescription: Path to the `pkg/` directory, e.g. `C:\Program Files\GAP-4.16.1\runtime\opt\gap-4.16.1\pkg` or `/opt/gap-4.16.1/pkg`.

enumDescriptions: Open a new terminal for each run.
gap.runMode.description: Terminal behavior when running a GAP file.

gap.terminalRoot.markdownDescription: Unix root for Windows drive letters. Example: `/` turns `C:\project\file.g` into `/c/project/file.g`. Leave empty to use WSL default `/mnt/`.

gap.docAppearance.description: Appearance of GAP documentation pages: 'system' follows the VS Code theme, 'dark'/'light' force a mode for all manuals.

gap.mathJax.description: Render math in GAP documentation pages with MathJax.

gap.searchMode.description: Search mode: prefix (?topic) matches from the start of a word, substring (??topic) matches anywhere

gap.diagnostics.description: Show syntax error diagnostics from the GAP parser in the Problems panel.

gap.tools.enabled.markdownDescription: Provide the native VS Code language model tools. Changes take effect immediately. Independent of `#gap.mcp.enabled#`; workspace settings can override user settings.

gap.mcp.enabled.markdownDescription: Enable the authenticated, loopback-only MCP service shared by trusted windows in this VS Code Profile. Configure in user settings; workspace overrides are ignored. Changes take effect across this Profile. Independent of `#gap.tools.enabled#`. The background service stops after the last participating window leaves.

gap.mcp.port.markdownDescription: One MCP port shared by windows in this VS Code Profile. Configure once in user settings; workspace overrides are ignored. Use `0` for one automatically allocated port while the service runs, or a fixed port for a stable external URL. Other Profiles, VS Code installations and unrelated programs cannot share this port. Changing it restarts the shared listener without changing the access token. A conflicting fixed port produces an error; no alternative port is chosen.

languageModelTools.name: search_gap_help
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search the GAP help index and get line locations
languageModelTools.modelDescription:
Searches GAP help and returns matched entries with their exact file location, so you can read the content with your built-in file-reading tool.

Response: { "results": [ { "index": int, "display": string, "type": "function"|"section"|"chapter"|"index"|omitted, "book": string, "absPath": string, "targetLine": int, "totalLines": int } ], "total": int, "returned": int, "note": string, "distribution": { book: int } }

- Each entry has 7 fields: index, display, type (omitted when there is no type code), book, absPath, targetLine, totalLines.
- index: 1-based position in the result list, stable within one index version.
- book: book short name; same as the books filter parameter and list_gap_books.
- absPath: absolute path of the entry's file; pass it directly to your file-reading tool.
- targetLine: 1-based start line; 0 means the entry has no anchor and covers the whole file.
- note: hints when there are special entries or invalid input.
- distribution: hit counts per book over ALL matches (global; independent of range), sorted descending; empty when there are no matches.

topic.description: Search word or phrase, as in ?topic (prefix) or ??topic (substring) in the GAP terminal. Must be non-empty. Special topics return no results: '-', '+', '&', '<', '>', '<<', '>>', 'books', 'chapters', 'contents', 'sections', 'welcome to gap', and digit-only topics (prefix mode only).

books.description: Book short names to search (get valid names from list_gap_books). Every name must be valid or the call is rejected.

range.description: 1-based inclusive [start, end] window of the result list, for paging. Defaults to [1, 20]; end > total is clamped, start > total returns empty results.

languageModelTools.name: list_gap_books
languageModelTools.modelDescription:
Lists all GAP help book short names; use these names in search_gap_help's books parameter.

Response: { "books": string[] }

languageModelTools.name: gap_resolve_link
languageModelTools.userDescription: Resolve a relative GAP help link to its absolute path and target line
languageModelTools.modelDescription:
Follows a relative link in a GAP help file and returns the target file's location, so you can read the linked page.

Response: { "targetPath": string, "targetLine": int, "totalLines": int, "anchor": string, "note": string }

- targetPath: absolute path of the target file (native separators; '../' resolved).
- targetLine: 1-based start line; 0 means no anchor, so read the whole file (line 1 to totalLines).
- note: empty when resolved successfully; otherwise explains why: missing anchor, target file not found, or external URL.

filePath.description: Absolute path of the GAP help file currently being read.

relativePath.description: The relative link (href) found in filePath; may contain '../'. External http(s) or mailto: URLs are not resolved; use a web tool or other tool for those.

anchor.description: Optional anchor to locate in the target file. Omitted, empty, or not found: targetLine is 0 and the whole file is read.

languageModelTools.name: check_gap_syntax
languageModelTools.userDescription: Statically check a GAP source file for syntax errors
languageModelTools.modelDescription:
Statically checks GAP source files for syntax errors using tree-sitter-gap.

Use this tool after creating or modifying a GAP source file, before running it.

The parser reports locations after error recovery, so they may not point to the root cause. A `Missing "X"` entry means the parser required `X` here but it is absent (e.g. a forgotten `;`); an `Unexpected syntax` entry often follows an unclosed construct near the reported location. If a reported location does not appear to explain the error, inspect the surrounding code context.

This tool provides preliminary static syntax checking only. It does not execute GAP code or perform semantic or logic checks, and is not a complete GAP interpreter validation or runtime diagnostic. `syntaxValid: true` means only that tree-sitter-gap reported no syntax errors; it does not guarantee that GAP itself will parse or execute the file without errors. Undefined variables, type errors, missing packages, and environment-dependent failures may still occur.

Input: { "filePath": string } — filePath must be the absolute path of the GAP source file to check.

Response: { "syntaxValid": boolean, "diagnostics": [ { "severity": "error", "line": int, "column": int, "message": string } ] }

- line and column are 1-based positions of the diagnostic range start.
- diagnostics is empty when syntaxValid is true.

filePath.description: Absolute path of the GAP source file to check. Relative paths are not accepted.

languageModelTools.name: run_gap_file
languageModelTools.userDescription: Run one GAP file in quiet, non-interactive mode with an optional working directory and redirect its output to a file
languageModelTools.modelDescription:
Runs exactly one GAP source file with GAP -q --nointeract in an independent process, in a trusted workspace. Saves unsaved changes if the file is open in the executing window.

Creates missing output parent directories and OVERWRITES an existing output file. Standard output and standard error are continuously redirected to outputPath while GAP runs; this tool does not return the log.

There is NO fixed runtime timeout: the invocation waits until the process exits or it is cancelled. Cancellation stops this invocation's process tree. Different output files may run concurrently, but concurrent writes to the same output file are rejected.

Response on normal process completion: { "completed": true }. Completion does NOT mean the GAP program succeeded. GAP-internal errors and nonzero exit codes are not interpreted as program success or failure; inspect outputPath yourself. Invalid paths, save/write/startup failures, or interruption are reported as tool errors rather than normal completion.

filePath.description: Absolute path of the single GAP source file to execute. Saves unsaved changes if this file is open.

outputPath.description: Absolute path of the output file. Overwrites it, creates missing parent directories, and writes stdout/stderr live. Read this path independently while execution is pending.

cwd.description: Optional absolute path to an existing directory in the extension host's filesystem. Sets the working directory for this invocation only. If omitted, uses the file's workspace root in the executing window, or the user's home directory on the extension host if the file does not belong to a workspace. Does not affect window selection. filePath and outputPath must still be absolute paths.
